title: fix(extension): harden bridge verb gating, handshake transport check and popup-request sender
body:
The security reviews of the #1323 extension splits (#1328, #1329) found three gaps. All three already exist on `main`, and none is exploitable today. The split PRs kept behaviour byte-identical on purpose, so these were left out of them.

## 1. Bridge verbs are gated on `connected`, not on `authenticated`
- **Where:** `apps/extension/src/lib/bridge/client.ts`, `session()`. Before #1329 the same check sat inline in every verb in `lib/bridge.ts`.
- **What happens:** `phase !== 'connected' || !transport` is the only seam a verb frame leaves through. With no stored token, `attach()` reaches `connected` without running a handshake.
- **Why it's safe today:** every background call site checks `getToken()` first.
- **Fix:** also require `authenticated` in `session()`, plus a test that sends a verb with no token stored.

## 2. Handshake sends `auth` to the live transport, not the one that issued the challenge
- **Where:** `apps/extension/src/lib/bridge/auth-handshake.ts`. After the proof `await`, the code checks only that a transport exists (`const live = this.host.transport(); if (!live) …`). The identity check comes later, just before `authenticated()`.
- **Impact:** practically unreachable and not exploitable. The proof is bound to the nonce, so a different peer rejects it and nothing leaks.
- **Fix:** add `if (live !== transport) return;`, plus a test that swaps the transport during the proof await.

## 3. The popup-request message path has no sender check
- **Where:** `apps/extension/src/background/message-listener.ts`, the `handleRequest(message as PopupRequest)` branch.
- **What happens:** any context of this extension, including its own content scripts, can send `setToken`, `documentAttach` and the other request kinds. Only `submitDetected` and open-panel-from-badge check `sender.id`.
- **Fix:** accept popup requests only when `sender.url` is an extension page, or gate per kind. Add tests for a content-script sender.

Refs #1323

title: chore(frontend): cap ts/tsx files at 300 code lines, split the large ones
body:
Follow-up to #1280, which applied the owner rule ("keep files small, under 300 lines") to the Rust backend. The Rust baselines are empty on `main` now. This issue applies the same rule to TypeScript/TSX.

## Scale (snapshot 2026-10-05, code lines only: blank and comment lines excluded, `.d.ts` excluded)

**129 of 1,569 tracked `.ts`/`.tsx` files are over 300 code lines.** 77 of them are test files.

| Band | Files |
|---|---|
| > 1,000 | 14 |
| 601–1,000 | 17 |
| 301–600 | 98 |

| Area | Files over 300 |
|---|---|
| `apps/desktop` (renderer) | 81 |
| `apps/extension` | 23 |
| `packages/prompts` | 8 |
| `packages/shared` | 7 |
| `packages/ui` | 6 |
| `apps/landing` | 4 |

Largest production files: `apps/landing/src/data/architecture-map.ts` (data), `apps/extension/src/lib/bridge.ts`, `apps/extension/src/background.ts`, `apps/desktop/src/renderer/features/applications/components/ApplicationDetailPage/index.tsx`, `apps/desktop/src/renderer/lib/generate/generation/generation.ts`. Largest tests: `apps/extension/src/{background,lib/bridge}.test.ts`, `renderer/lib/generate/generation/generation.test.ts`, `packages/prompts/src/generate/generate.test.ts`.

These counts are a dated snapshot. The guard below generates the live list.

## Proposal (same shape as #1280)
1. **Guard first.** Use ESLint core `max-lines` with `{ max: 300, skipBlankLines: true, skipComments: true }` for every `.ts`/`.tsx` file, tests included, plus a generated ratchet baseline. A baselined file may shrink but never grow. A new file over the cap fails. A stale entry fails. A bless flag regenerates the baseline. Add the rule to `AGENTS.md` beside rule 18.
2. **Split by responsibility, and shrink while splitting.** Same DRY/KISS/SOLID/YAGNI rule as #1280. Behaviour and test assertions stay unchanged, and each PR's net code-line delta must go down. Components split into sub-components and hooks inside their own feature dir (rule 9: never across feature dirs). Large test suites become `<name>/<topic>.test.ts(x)` with shared fixtures.
3. **Decide on data files.** `architecture-map.ts` is a declarative node table. Either split it per cluster or give it a reasoned exception (the Rust side has `R8_EXCEPTIONS` for this).
4. **One area per PR, largest first:** extension (`bridge.ts`, `background.ts`, their tests) → renderer features → `renderer/lib/generate` → `packages/{prompts,shared,ui}` → landing.

## Plan
- [x] PR 0: guard + baseline + `AGENTS.md` rule (#1325, hardened in #1326)
- [x] PR 1: `apps/extension` — 1a bridge (#1329) · 1b background (#1328) · 1c the rest (#1330)
- [ ] PR 2+: `apps/desktop/src/renderer` (split by feature)
- [ ] PR n: `packages/*`
- [ ] PR n+1: `apps/landing`
- [ ] Docs sync
